text: My main symptom is Aggressive cough with thick, yellow-green sputum. I also have Cough worse in the morning, History of recurrent bronchitis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia (PCD).

The clinical picture of an 11-year history of chronic "bronchitis" in a non-smoker, characterized by copious foamy sputum and morning predominance, is classic for a mucociliary clearance defect rather than infectious bronchitis or asthma. Given the lack of reported sinus or dental issues, I suspect the sinus involvement may be subtle or underreported; however, the sputum description is highly specific.

I will proceed with the diagnosis based on the strong clinical evidence of impaired mucociliary clearance despite the pending imaging.
